content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text rests an UNDERDETERMINED finding on a single verse's wording.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings", "rule_words": "A judge may not rest STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED on one verse failing to state a link or its contrary.", "room": "'failing to state a link or its contrary': read one way, a verse that 'admits both readings' is exactly a verse that states neither the link nor its contrary, so resting UNDERDETERMINED on it is barred; read the other way, the rule bars only resting on silence about the link, not on a verse whose grammar positively supports both readings. The first reading fits both the rule's words and the definition's clause that 'a verse that admits both readings decides nothing by itself.'", "why": "The judge rests the UNDERDETERMINED on Matthew 1:16 alone, on the ground that it admits both readings rather than stating the link or its contrary, which is what K-S2 forbids; the closing references to the sides' answers name no additional support for the UNDERDETERMINED itself."}
